title: approved-apps
description: The applications and services a cabinet may be asked to control (docs/spec/13-roadmap.md: process.end and app.restart with a per-client allowlist). One entry pins the exact program: the executable path is written by an owner and never by a Tier 1 or Tier 2 account, by the console's write path or by the agent. A server administrator sets the list for the fleet, a client, a site or a cabinet through the device-settings route, with step-up and an audit entry. entries null removes that level's list so the level above applies; an empty list means control nothing at this level.

level.description: The level the list is set for. The most specific level with a list wins whole for a cabinet.

id.description: The client, site or cabinet id; null for the fleet (level fleet).

entries.description: At most 32 approved programs. An application is pinned by its executable path alone; a service is pinned by its registered executable path AND its service name, so a service that has been replaced by something else of the same name is not controlled by mistake.

key.description: The baseline item key this program stands for, in the applications category (app:<name>), so its version can be compared with the site's baseline. No separators, no control characters.

kind.description: application: started by its path (app.restart). service: controlled through the service control manager (service.control, and process.end of the process it runs as).

name.description: What the owner calls it, shown in the console. Text only: it is never a path and never an argument.

stepUpToken.description: A one-time step-up token bound to this exact action, level and these exact entries.
